title: The Deep Breath Before the Cannonball
skyStory: Last day of the moon's swim through Pisces, and it is getting restless, twenty-eight percent bright and splashing toward the edge of the pool. Tomorrow it climbs out into Aries and things get loud. Today is the deep breath before the cannonball. Saturn checks the ice on the pond. Thick enough. Mars is already lacing up skates.

reading: Your Aries moon arrives tomorrow and you can already feel it, like the hum before a thunderstorm. Use today to clear the runway. Close three browser tabs. Answer the message you have been avoiding. Put away the thing that has been sitting on the chair for nine days. You know the chair.

Late afternoon you will catch yourself standing like a superhero for no reason, hands on hips, gazing into the middle distance. Lean in. [[The Chariot]] is warming up its engine, and tomorrow you will want every horse in the stable. Tonight, turn in eleven minutes earlier than usual. Mars will complain. Ignore him.
joel.mission: Clear the chair. You know the chair. Everything on it goes back where it belongs before dinner.
joel.omen: Skates hanging on a hook or a fence. It means you are about to glide through something you expected to be clumsy.

reading: The pond near the shore has frozen into a perfect grey mirror, and today you get to be brave in a small, slippery way. Try one thing you are slightly afraid of looking silly doing. A new phrase in another language. A dance move in the kitchen. A question in a meeting.

The [[Strength]] card shows a gentle hand on a lion's head. You do not need to roar today. You just need to keep your balance with a little grace, which you have always had. If you wobble, laugh. Wobbling while laughing is the most powerful pose in the known universe.
nancy.mission: Do one thing you are a little afraid of looking silly doing, in front of at least one witness.
nancy.omen: A child skating with arms wide open. It means joy is about to beat caution, and that is excellent news.

together.text: Each of you does one tiny brave thing today and reports back in exactly five words. Not four. Not six. Five. Saturn will count. If either of you goes over, you both owe the universe a goofy selfie in a winter hat.
